newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to host conference on thinking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to host conference on thinking.

text.p: Singapore will host an international conference on thinking in June 1997, a spokeswoman for the National Institute of Education (NIE) said on Friday.

The conference, to be attended by more than 2,000 academics and business leaders, will discuss how different thinking processes work and how they can be taught, NIE senior fellow Norah Maier told Reuters.
The pioneer of the idea of lateral thinking, Edward de Bono, would be among the more than 150 speakers at the gathering, Maier said.
The announcement of the conference follows a recent move by the Singapore government to promote innovative thinking skills in schools.
Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said in September his government would spend Singapore $1.5 billion (US$1.06 billion) over the next five years on the programme.
The move was a response to complaints from local employers that Singaporean school-leavers and graduates were better copiers than creators and had problems working independently.
"We need creativity in our thinking to be competitive," said Maier.
